name: Cartagena
tagline: Caribbean Charm, Colonial Beauty, and Remarkable Affordability
description: Cartagena is a jewel of the Caribbean coast — a UNESCO World Heritage walled city with colorful colonial architecture, warm turquoise waters, and a vibrant cultural scene rooted in Afro-Caribbean, Spanish, and indigenous traditions. The cost of living is remarkably low, healthcare is surprisingly good through Colombia's well-regarded system, and the food scene blends fresh seafood with tropical flavors. While English is limited and the tropical heat is relentless, Cartagena rewards adventurous retirees with a rich, affordable, and deeply atmospheric life.

quickFacts.visa: 90-day visa-free for US citizens (extendable to 180 days); retirement visa available
quickFacts.safetyRating: Moderate – safe in tourist areas; standard urban precautions advised
quickFacts.climate: Tropical with year-round heat and a rainy season from May to November

housing.description: Frugal furnished studio or 1BR in Getsemaní or the residential edge of Centro; respects the walled-city/tourist rent floor (not the rock-bottom local level)

dining.description: Almuerzo corriente and local seafood plates a few times a week plus street food

healthcare.description: EPS contributory plus a basic prepagada / entry Colsanitas-Sura plan; priced for a healthy 45–55

transportation.description: Buses, mototaxi, and InDrive; the historic center is walkable

entertainment.description: Beach days, sea-wall walks, salsa, an occasional gym visit

1M.lifestyle: A frugal furnished studio or one-bedroom in Getsemaní or the residential fringe of the old center puts colonial streets, the sea wall, and market stalls within walking distance. Days lean on almuerzo corriente, fresh ceviche from a neighborhood spot, and produce from the mercado, with mototaxis and buses covering the rest. The air conditioning runs sparingly to keep the electricity bill down against the relentless coastal heat, and cover is an entry Colombian prepagada plan. Beach afternoons and free walks along the ramparts fill the calendar. A genuinely economical life, though the tourist-enclave rent floor keeps housing from collapsing to bare-local levels.

housing.description: Comfortable furnished 1BR in Getsemaní or lower Bocagrande with reliable A/C

dining.description: Out several times a week: ceviche bars, mid-range tables, rooftop drinks

transportation.description: Regular taxi/InDrive plus occasional Rosario Islands boat trips

entertainment.description: Island hopping, salsa lessons, gym, cultural festivals

2M.lifestyle: A comfortable furnished apartment in Getsemaní or lower Bocagrande, with air conditioning that runs all day, anchors an easy coastal routine. Eating out is regular — ceviche bars, mid-range kitchens, sunset drinks on a rooftop — and the health plan steps up to a comprehensive prepagada with good clinic access. Weekends bring boat trips to the Rosario Islands and the occasional escape to the cooler Sierra Nevada. Comprehensive but unpretentious, this budget goes a long way on the Caribbean coast.

housing.description: Prime furnished 1BR in the Walled City / Centro Histórico or an upper-Bocagrande unit with quality A/C

dining.description: Frequent good restaurants, Carmen/Celele occasionally, premium cocktail bars

healthcare.description: Top-tier prepagada (premium Colsanitas) plus a supplement

transportation.description: Regular car service/InDrive, island boat access, occasional domestic flight

entertainment.description: Island day trips, diving, cultural events, domestic travel across Colombia

3M.lifestyle: A prime furnished apartment inside the Walled City's colonial streets, or a high-floor Bocagrande unit with sea breezes, sets the tone for a well-appointed early-retirement life. Dining is frequent and good — standout kitchens like Carmen and Celele are within reach — and the health plan is a top prepagada with a supplement. Island boat trips, diving, and domestic flights to Bogotá, Medellín, or coffee country open up the calendar. This sits comfortably above what most residents of the city spend, with real headroom in the budget.

housing.description: An entire restored colonial house in the Walled City or a luxury beachfront penthouse in Bocagrande/Castillogrande (long-term rate)

dining.description: Fine dining regularly, occasional private-chef meals, premium wine

healthcare.description: Entry international plan (Cigna Global / GeoBlue tier) for a 45–55

transportation.description: Car with driver, private-boat access, domestic first-class

domesticHelp.description: Near-full-time housekeeper-cook (Colombian all-in wages run higher in USD at the strong 2026 peso; Cartagena rates sit ~15% above Medellín)

luxuryExtras.description: Standing travel fund, club memberships, discretionary

5M.lifestyle: An entire restored colonial house behind the ramparts, or a luxury beachfront penthouse with an infinity pool in Bocagrande, comes with household help several days a week. Fine dining is routine, an international health plan replaces the local prepagada, and a driver plus private-boat access make island days effortless. The discretionary budget funds yacht charters, cultural patronage, and a standing travel fund. A polished, well-staffed version of coastal life that runs well beyond the local cost base.

housing.description: A grand colonial mansion in Centro Histórico or a private beachfront villa compound on Barú / near the Rosario Islands (long-term equivalent)

dining.description: Uncapped fine dining, imported wine cellar, lavish entertaining

healthcare.description: International concierge plan with medical evacuation (worldwide, priced for a 45–55)

transportation.description: Multiple vehicles with driver, private-boat/yacht access, chartered/first-class flights

entertainment.description: Yacht charters, private-island retreats, deep-sea fishing, cultural events

domesticHelp.description: Resident household staff: a housekeeper-cook plus a gardener-caretaker with a driver on call (roughly two full-time-equivalent workers, benefits included)

luxuryExtras.description: Private-jet access, art acquisition, major philanthropy, uncapped discretionary

10M.lifestyle: A grand colonial estate inside the historic walls, or a private beachfront villa compound out toward Barú and the Rosario Islands, kept by resident household staff — a housekeeper-cook and a gardener-caretaker with a driver on call. Dining is uncapped, with an imported cellar and lavish entertaining, and healthcare is a worldwide concierge plan with medical evacuation. Multiple vehicles, private-boat access, and chartered or first-class flights handle movement, and the discretionary budget stretches to art, yacht charters, and philanthropy across the region. This is the top of what the Colombian Caribbean offers, well beyond anything the local market requires.
